title: Primitive-element polynomial presentation after field base change
statement: Let $K/k$ and $E/k$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension], with $E/k$ finite separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; finite means finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. There exist $\alpha\in E$ and $P\in k[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] such that $E=k(\alpha)$, $P$ is the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k$, $P$ is monic and irreducible, and $\deg P\geq1$. Write $P_K$ for its coefficientwise image in $K[T]$ [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map]. There is a $K$-algebra isomorphism $\Phi:K\otimes_k E\xrightarrow{\sim}K[T]/(P_K)$, where the tensor algebra [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] has multiplication $(a\otimes e)(b\otimes f)=ab\otimes ef$, and $(P_K)$ is the ideal of multiples of $P_K$. For all $a\in K$ and $g\in k[T]$, $\Phi(a\otimes g(\alpha))=[a g_K(T)]$, where $g_K$ is the coefficientwise image of $g$. Its inverse sends every coefficient class $[a]$ to $a\otimes1$ and $[T]$ to $1\otimes\alpha$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-primitive-element] to the finite separable extension $E/k$, obtaining $\alpha$ with $E=k(\alpha)$. Every element of $E$ is algebraic by [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; take $P$ to be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$. It is monic by the minimal-polynomial definition. Explicitly, if $P=uv$ with both factors nonunits, both have positive degree smaller than $\deg P$; the field identity $0=P(\alpha)=u(\alpha)v(\alpha)$ forces one factor to vanish at $\alpha$, contradicting minimality. Thus $P$ is irreducible, consistently with the characterization in the cited statement. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso], $\deg P\geq1$ and evaluation induces a $k$-algebra isomorphism $e:k[T]/(P)\to E$, $[g]\mapsto g(\alpha)$. In particular every element of $E$ is $g(\alpha)$ for some $g\in k[T]$.

proof.text: Put $B=K[T]/(P_K)$ and $z=[T]\in B$, with its coefficient $K$-algebra structure. If $P=\sum_i c_iT^i$, then $\sum_i[c_i]z^i=[P_K]=0$, so $z$ is a root of $P$ in the $k$-algebra $B$. Apply [lem-asd-polynomial-quotient-hom-equivalence] with $R=k$, $C=B$, $f=P$ to obtain $u:k[T]/(P)\to B$ satisfying $u([g])=[g_K]$. The composite $j=u\circ e^{-1}:E\to B$ is a $k$-algebra homomorphism and satisfies $j(g(\alpha))=[g_K]$ for every $g\in k[T]$.

source.place: Tag 037P (lemma-field-extension-geometrically-irreducible), proof, displayed tensor-quotient identification; explicit universal-property assembly by Q54

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], $A=K\otimes_k E$ is a commutative algebra with $(a\otimes e)(b\otimes f)=ab\otimes ef$, with coefficient map $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and right inclusion $e\mapsto1\otimes e$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property] with $R=k$, $S=K$, algebra $E$ and target $B$ to the map $j$ of step 2. It gives a $K$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi:A\to B$ satisfying $\Phi(a\otimes g(\alpha))=[a]\,j(g(\alpha))=[a g_K]$. In particular $\Phi(1\otimes\alpha)=z$.

source.place: Tag 037P (lemma-field-extension-geometrically-irreducible), proof, displayed tensor-quotient identification; explicit universal-property assembly by Q54

proof.text: Let $t=1\otimes\alpha\in A$. The right inclusion $E\to A$ is a $k$-algebra homomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. For $P=\sum_i c_iT^i$ this gives $P_K(t)=\sum_i(c_i\otimes1)(1\otimes\alpha^i)=\sum_i1\otimes c_i\alpha^i=1\otimes P(\alpha)=0$; the middle identity uses the balancing relation defining the tensor product. Apply [lem-asd-polynomial-quotient-hom-equivalence] with $R=K$, $C=A$, $f=P_K$ and root $t$. It gives a $K$-algebra homomorphism $\Psi:B\to A$ with $\Psi([\sum_i a_iT^i])=\sum_i(a_i\otimes1)t^i$. Consequently $\Psi([a])=a\otimes1$ and $\Psi(z)=1\otimes\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 037P (lemma-field-extension-geometrically-irreducible), proof, displayed tensor-quotient identification; explicit universal-property assembly by Q54

proof.text: For every $g=\sum_i c_iT^i\in k[T]$, the formulas above give $\Psi([g_K])=\sum_i(c_i\otimes1)t^i=1\otimes g(\alpha)$. Thus $\Psi\Phi$ and $\mathrm{id}_A$ have the same restrictions to $E$, since step 1 represents every element as $g(\alpha)$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property] implies $\Psi\Phi=\mathrm{id}_A$. Also $\Phi\Psi(z)=\Phi(t)=z$, so uniqueness in [lem-asd-polynomial-quotient-hom-equivalence], now for $R=K$, $C=B$ and $f=P_K$, gives $\Phi\Psi=\mathrm{id}_B$. Hence $\Phi$ is the required $K$-algebra isomorphism with inverse $\Psi$ and all the asserted formulas.
